summary:
The "Prove It Act of 2024" (H.R. 7198, 118th Congress), as passed by the House on December 5, 2024, and received in the Senate on December 9, 2024, amends Chapter 6 of title 5, U.S. Code (the Regulatory Flexibility Act), to expand small-entity impact disclosure requirements and create a new petition-and-review mechanism administered by the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Small Business Administration.

Section 2 amends § 603(b) to add a new paragraph (6) requiring each initial regulatory flexibility analysis, "where feasible," to identify reasonably foreseeable indirect costs on small entities, including entities transacting with directly regulated entities, entities regulated by other governmental bodies as a result of the rule, and entities subject to other agency rules as a result of the rule. It amends § 605(b) to impose a 10-day deadline (after certification) for the agency to publish a certification that a proposed rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

Section 2 also adds a new § 605A establishing a petition process. Any small entity, group, or representative organization may petition the Chief Counsel to review a § 605(b) certification; the section specifies petition form, content, and consultation procedures (with the Chief Counsel barred from advising whether to amend or withdraw). The Chief Counsel must conduct a prima facie review within 10 days: if the petition lacks merit, the matter is closed; if it merits review, the Chief Counsel notifies the petitioner and agency and undertakes a full review. Full review requires specified considerations, a mandatory meeting (including OIRA's Administrator), and publication of results in the Federal Register and on the Office of Advocacy website within 30 days. If the Chief Counsel determines a significant impact exists, the agency must perform initial and final regulatory flexibility analyses under §§ 603 and 604. As a penalty, if an agency fails to attend the required meeting or otherwise fails to assist, the final rule "shall not apply to small entities." For chapter 7 judicial review, the certification becomes final agency action upon a no-further-review determination or publication of full-review results.

Section 3 adds § 609(f), requiring agencies, for rules likely to have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, to publish guidance and related documents on regulations.gov (or similar) and allow comment.

Section 4 amends § 610 to require periodic review to address indirect costs (new paragraph (6)) and adds subsection (d): if an agency fails to complete required 10-year review, the rule ceases to be effective, subject to a Federal Register notification, comment solicitation, and a 180-day reinstatement review (bypassing § 553 procedures). Section 4's subsection (a)(2) amendment applies to final rules issued during the 5-year period preceding enactment or thereafter. The Act contains no appropriation.
